question: Can Gradle replace the proposed Cook execution engine while retaining useful repository migrations?
prerequisites: JDK 17 or newer compatible with Gradle 9.8.1

inputs.offlineInstall: true for the local dependency fixture
inputs.awsRole: Role ARN or GitHub expression; default vars.BUILD_AWS_ROLE_ARN

fixtures.node: Minimal runnable project with a local dependency; not a copy of a production manifest
fixtures.aws: medprev-rest-api workflows, with explicit permissions added to the selected job and caller for this experiment
fixtures.aws-legacy: Unchanged workflow copies used to prove implicit permissions are rejected
fixtures.combined: Synthetic independent Node and AWS jobs; composed from node plus combined fixtures

scope: Native Gradle plugin, task graph, lazy providers and incremental task inputs/outputs
Two concrete migrations with native files
Saved diff, separate apply, drift rejection
No AWS calls; role and trust policy must exist separately
New lockfile resolved by target package manager; equivalence to previous dependency resolution is not guaranteed
limitations: Known layouts only; not a general repository migrator
Snapshot includes only explicit file patterns from build.gradle
No migration of Dockerfiles, arbitrary shell scripts, monorepos or private registry auth
No automatic ownership discovery, rollback after a process crash, or personal setup/session lifecycle
No assumption that the chosen AWS permission baseline fits every repository
Combining the Node switch with the existing medprev AWS build is refused: it still uses npm and npm-specific CodeArtifact authentication
